newsitem.title: GERMANY: Floods would not damage E.German farmland for long.
newsitem.headline: Floods would not damage E.German farmland for long.

text.p: Flooded arable land in the eastern German state of Brandenburg should not suffer lasting damage from toxic metals or leaking mineral oils tanks, a Bonn environment ministry spokesman said on Monday.
The sheer size of water volumes would dilute the effect of damaging materials carried by the floods, he said in response to enquiries.
But he saw as-yet unspecified dangers from E. coli bacteria, which could cause damage to animal intestines and could reach the human food chain.
Water levels in the Oderbruch basin, a low lying area of 850 square kilometres, are rising by the hour and some 9,000 people may be evacuated at a moment's notice.
Large sections of the dike protecting the Oderbruch have collapsed over the past few days and an estimated several thousands of hectares are already flooded.
On Friday, some 5,000 people were evacuated from the most endangered area near Hohenwutzen at the north end of the Oderbruch area.
At risk of flooding are up to 76,165 hectares of fertile farmland -- roughly the size of Hamburg -- the Brandenburg state farm ministry said earlier on Monday.
The grain harvest from 41,332 ha in the region was disrupted by farmers' evacuations and participation in the fight against the floods.
It may wait up to another six weeks but irregular harvesting means quality and volume losses are certain, regional farm sources said.
Yet this is dwarfed by Germany's anticipated 42-43 million tonne grain harvest this year. The national grain area totals 7.04 million ha.

Brandenburg farm union (DBV) president Heinz-Dieter Nieschke said the evacuation of pigs and dairy cows would cause losses because stressed animals could need to be slaughtered. High-performance cows with a 7,000 litre milk output per year need milking every day but this could not be guaranteed if they were temporarily kept in makeshift sheds.
